paper_summary: The paper studies the formal expressive power gained when decoder-only transformers use intermediate chain-of-thought tokens, proving automata and Turing-machine simulation results.

claimed_contributions.text: Formalizes transformer decoding with intermediate tokens.
Constructs simulations of finite automata and Turing machines.
Provides upper and lower bounds for decoder expressiveness.

claim_checks.claim_text: Intermediate decoding strictly expands transformer computational expressiveness under the stated model.
claim_checks.reasoning: Judged only against the paper's own methods, results and stated limitations.

claim_checks.claim_text: The constructed transformer can simulate bounded-time Turing computation.

overall_assessment: A theoretically substantial paper with explicit constructions and a clear separation between direct and intermediate decoding. Dense notation and distributed appendices reduce usability, while the proof-focused nature makes several experimental checklist items inapplicable.
strengths: Formulates a precise theoretical question rather than treating chain of thought only empirically.
Provides constructive lower bounds through automata and Turing-machine simulations.
Separates assumptions and places detailed constructions in appendices.
concerns: The relationship between idealized precision/attention assumptions and deployed transformers is limited.
Dense notation makes the proof path difficult to audit quickly.
No executable proof artifact or implementation is identified in the assessed version.
unresolved_questions: Which results survive finite-precision and soft-attention constraints?
Can the constructions predict practical scaling behavior?
limitations_of_this_assessment: No experiment or code was executed.
Originality evaluates the paper's positioning rather than an exhaustive prior-art search.
